title: I2S Protocol Timing Explorer
description: A logic-analyzer view of BCLK, WS, and SD on a shared time axis with bit-by-bit stepping, channel shading, and an assembled-word readout.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Embedded Systems
Serial Protocols

learningObjectives: Examine the timing relationship between BCLK, WS, and SD
Distinguish left-channel bits from right-channel bits
Relate word length to the number of BCLK pulses per WS half-cycle
prerequisites: A digital signal is high or low over time

controls.label: Bit back / Bit forward
controls.purpose: Move the playhead one BCLK pulse

controls.label: Next word boundary
controls.purpose: Jump directly to the next WS transition

assumptions: Fixed example data words so the pattern is stable while stepping
Idealized edges with no setup/hold time or propagation delay
Standard I2S phase; left-justified and right-justified variants are not shown
limitations: Does not model the one-BCLK data delay of the original Philips frame format, nor multi-slot TDM modes

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Manual step-through of a multi-signal timing diagram
keyQuestions: Is WS a pulse at the boundary, or a level held across the word?
How many BCLK pulses occur per WS half-cycle at 24-bit?
commonMisconceptions: That WS pulses briefly at each word boundary rather than holding a level
That SD alone is enough to decode the stream
assessmentOpportunities: Given a described trace, count the samples and total audio bits captured
